races.name: St. Austell Brewery Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dunaden Island
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 40-day break with solid placed form, should track the early pace effectively

runners_data.name: Queens Up
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up type whose lack of recent form creates uncertainty but could benefit from race fitness

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 7-day turnaround advantage, headgear applied suggests connections expect improvement

runners_data.name: Onefournine
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with winning form, 71-day break could be either refreshing or concerning

runners_data.name: Jolissaint
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with poor recent form including a fall, needs significant improvement from current level

runners_data.name: Kaydence
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form, 40-day break allows time to recover from busy autumn campaign

runners_data.name: Bits Ballou
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in finish, needs strong early pace to set up her closing kick

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with highest rating, proven at good ground and ideal for controlled gallop

runners_data.name: Davita Blaze
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from 20-day break, recent fifth suggests she needs to find improvement

runners_data.name: Fountains Gala
runners_data.note: Lightly raced type who fades late, 40-day break provides freshness but form remains questionable

races.paceDynamic: Onefournine emerges as the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the start, with several prominent racers like Laffer Curve, Dunaden Island, and Davita Blaze tracking close behind. The lack of multiple pace pressers means Onefournine can control the tempo without being bustled along early. The extended 2m5½f trip allows hold-up horses like Stavanger Rose, Kaydence, and Bits Ballou to settle off the pace before making their moves. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to Onefournine's controlled gallop and kick when the pace lifts, rather than pure front runners or deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Onefournine maintains steady fractions without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows prominent racers to conserve energy and deliver sustained challenges from the home turn. Higher-rated horses like Laffer Curve and the in-form Onefournine can utilise their class advantage in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian allowing hold-up horses time to organise
scenarios.body: Kaydence and Stavanger Rose get the patient ride they need before unleashing finishing kicks that overwhelm the prominently-raced horses. The extended trip plays perfectly into their stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Onefournine's recent win provides the confidence to stretch the field from halfway
scenarios.body: The 71-day break proves beneficial as Onefournine kicks clear turning for home while prominent racers struggle to bridge the gap. Her proven form at this trip becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent racers fail to pressure Onefournine creating a crawling pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the final furlong heavily favouring horses with natural speed regardless of running style. Fresh legs and tactical positioning matter more than stamina.

watchPoints.text: Onefournine must handle the 71-day layoff after her impressive last win, any early rustiness could derail her chance
Queens Up represents the biggest unknown having been absent since May, market confidence will reveal connections' expectations
Stavanger Rose applies headgear for the first time suggesting trainer expects the equipment to spark improvement
The pace could become pedestrian if prominent racers show Onefournine too much respect early
Laffer Curve's consistent form makes her the reliable each-way option if the pace develops favourably

races.name: Newton Abbot Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: No Panic
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with clear pace angle but recent form shows vulnerability when pressured, 22 days since last run could aid freshness

runners_data.name: Bredon Hill Dart
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse for in-form Sue Gardner yard, excellent recent form including a win, well-suited to tactical race shape

runners_data.name: Albert Park
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor recent form is major concern, needs to rediscover best form from earlier in career

runners_data.name: Green Asset
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 149-day break for Mickey Bowen, strong previous form suggests well-handicapped if retaining ability

runners_data.name: Masonbrook Meadow
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for in-form Seamus Mullins yard, 125 days off but has winning form over course and distance

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in three slow-ground hurdles but may fare better on this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three slow-ground maiden/novice hurdles this year (2m-2m4f; latest run was stable debut) but came second in two 3m Irish points last April (good/yielding) and looks interesting now back up in trip and back on forecast good ground for this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Gilded Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but concerning recent form downturn, needs significant improvement to feature prominently

runners_data.name: Keepkalmandkarryon
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with poor recent form, 21 days since disappointing last effort suggests little confidence

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Paul Nicholls but form figures show consistency issues, 36-day break could help

runners_data.name: Tobi Kanobee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with decent RPR rating, 22 days since last run and previous course form offers hope

races.paceDynamic: No Panic looks the clear pace-setter with his prominent style and confirmed front-running tendencies, likely to dictate from the outset. The majority of this field are hold-up horses (Bredon Hill Dart, Green Asset, Masonbrook Meadow, Gilded Glance, Keepkalmandkarryon) who will need the pace to develop. With limited early pace pressure from just No Panic, Albert Park, Jetty May and Tobi Kanobee up front, this sets up as a tactical affair that will strongly favour the hold-up horses who can produce a finishing kick when the tempo lifts in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If No Panic sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate through the early stages
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash late runs, with Bredon Hill Dart and Green Asset best positioned to capitalise. The prominent runners find themselves outpaced when the race develops into a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Battle
scenarios.trigger: If No Panic and Albert Park engage in early pace pressure, creating stronger gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The increased tempo plays into the hands of the other prominent runners who can track the pace without being caught up in the early battle. Tobi Kanobee and Jetty May benefit from the honest pace to show their best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling slow with all hold-up horses waiting too long to make their moves
scenarios.body: No Panic and Albert Park benefit from the lack of finishing kick in the field, maintaining their advantage to the line. The hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the pace dynamics create chaos with the favoured runners cancelling each other out
scenarios.body: An unfancied hold-up horse like Keepkalmandkarryon or Makinbrook Meadow capitalises on the tactical battle ahead of them. The field comes back to the outsiders who have been patiently tracking the leading group.

watchPoints.text: No Panic must be watched for early pace-setting role - if he goes too fast early he'll set it up perfectly for the hold-up horses
Green Asset's fitness after 149 days off is crucial - any market support would indicate connections expect him ready to run well
Bredon Hill Dart's jumping under pressure will be key given her hold-up style requires clean hurdling to maintain position for late challenge
The early pace battle between No Panic and Albert Park will determine whether this becomes tactical or end-to-end
Masonbrook Meadow's return from 125-day layoff needs monitoring - any positive body language would suggest significant each-way claims

races.name: Thatchers Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Uncle Phil
runners_data.note: Front runner with solid recent form but 26 days off and carrying top weight of 170lbs could tell against younger rivals

runners_data.name: Siam Park
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter with strong recent RPR of 125 and useful 21-day break, but faces pace pressure from two other leaders

runners_data.name: Raffles Hermes
runners_data.note: Third front runner gets weight relief at 156lbs but poor trainer record (0/3 in last 14 days) and 31 days since last run

runners_data.name: Irish Chorus
runners_data.note: Only hold-up runner perfectly positioned to benefit from the inevitable pace battle, with excellent recent winning form and tactical advantage

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Phil, Siam Park and Raffles Hermes will all want the early lead in this small field, creating a strong gallop from the start. With three confirmed front runners and only Irish Chorus racing from behind, the pace will be honest throughout with no let-up. The sustained gallop over 2m½f will test stamina reserves as the leaders battle for supremacy. This race shape strongly favours Irish Chorus with his hold-up style, as he can benefit from the pace collapse when the three leaders weaken each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too fast early and weaken each other significantly
scenarios.body: Irish Chorus gets the perfect setup as Tom Bellamy can track the strong pace and pounce when the front runners tire. His recent winning form and hold-up style are perfectly suited to capitalize on pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can find enough left in the tank after setting strong fractions
scenarios.body: Siam Park or Uncle Phil could prove tough enough to see off their rivals despite the pace pressure. The winner would need exceptional stamina reserves to withstand both the early battle and late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders unexpectedly steady the pace early to avoid mutual destruction
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with a sprint finish, potentially suiting whichever front runner has most left. Irish Chorus loses his main advantage if the pace becomes moderate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go so fast they all stop dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Irish Chorus wins easily as the only horse with energy left, but this requires an extreme pace scenario. The front runners would need to completely misjudge their effort distribution.

watchPoints.text: Watch if any of the three leaders (Uncle Phil, Siam Park, Raffles Hermes) tries to steal an early advantage as this will intensify the pace battle
Monitor Irish Chorus early positioning as Tom Bellamy must not get too far back with only four runners
Check if Raffles Hermes shows early sharpness after 31 days off as rustiness could remove one pace angle
Watch Uncle Phil under top weight as 170lbs may prove decisive if the pace is as strong as expected
Observe if Siam Park's recent good form translates to stamina reserves needed for a sustained battle

races.name: Tribute Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who should track Lightonthewing perfectly and benefits from Joe Tizzard's good strike rate

runners_data.name: Welcheston Warrier
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent recent course form at Newton Abbot, headgear retained suggests confidence after 38-day break

runners_data.name: Lightonthewing
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who gets uncontested lead but 11-year-old faces stamina test after 19 days since Fontwell success

runners_data.name: Dearkeithandkaty
runners_data.note: Classy hold-up horse with strong recent form, headgear applied suggests connections expect improvement from this talented 5-year-old

runners_data.name: I Love You Sivola
runners_data.note: Prominent runner completely outclassed on ratings and poor recent form suggests vulnerable against this stronger field

runners_data.name: My Own Lovely Lee
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 39-day break with headgear retained but recent soft ground form may not translate to good conditions

races.paceDynamic: Lightonthewing will dictate terms from the front with his confirmed lead style, likely getting an uncontested gallop given the lack of other genuine pace angles. Striking A Pose may track in second but prefers to sit prominent rather than challenge early, while the three hold-up horses (Welcheston Warrier, Dearkeithandkaty, My Own Lovely Lee) will sit off the pace. This creates a moderate tempo with kick potential, as Lightonthewing can control fractions without pressure until the business end. The race shape clearly favours the prominent/tracking runners who can sit close enough to strike when the pace lifts, rather than front-runners who may tire or hold-up horses facing a potentially inadequate pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Lightonthewing sets steady fractions without early pressure from Striking A Pose
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop suits horses tracking in behind who can quicken off the bend, with enough pace to prevent a sprint finish but not so much as to empty the tank. Striking A Pose and Dearkeithandkaty benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Lightonthewing's rivals fail to close quickly enough turning for home
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old uses his early advantage and recent Fontwell win confidence to repel late challenges, especially with the good going helping his stamina reserves. His soft lead becomes decisive when others leave their runs too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong with Striking A Pose pressing Lightonthewing earlier than expected
scenarios.body: A faster tempo sets up perfectly for the three hold-up runners who can finish strongly up the hill, with Welcheston Warrier's recent Newton Abbot form and Dearkeithandkaty's class shining through. The pace collapse favours patient tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Into Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Lightonthewing sets very sedate fractions and the field remains bunched turning in
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where tactical positioning matters more than stamina, potentially suiting any horse with a strong turn of foot regardless of usual style. Fresh legs and good jumping become crucial in a cavalry charge.

watchPoints.text: Lightonthewing could get too soft a lead early and prove hard to peg back if allowed to dictate fractions completely unchallenged
Striking A Pose's jumping under pressure - any mistakes when trying to close on the leader could prove costly in small field
Welcheston Warrier needs the hold-up tactics to work perfectly as he's most dependent on pace collapse to be effective
Dearkeithandkaty's headgear change signals intent and this unexposed 5-year-old could have more improvement to come
Watch for how quickly the pace develops early - if Striking A Pose tracks closer than usual it changes the entire complexion

races.name: Visit Kauto The King 6th May Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tapley
runners_data.note: Recent winner with strong course form who should track the leader and challenge late under inexperienced rider Isabelle Ryder.

runners_data.name: Hold Up La Colmine
runners_data.note: Consistent placer seeking breakthrough win but hasn't won for over a year despite regular placing efforts.

runners_data.name: Soldierofthestorm
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can control this small field from the front but hasn't won since March 2023.

runners_data.name: Clotilda
runners_data.note: Young improving type for powerful Nicholls stable but concerning recent fall and 47 days absence raises fitness questions.

runners_data.name: Sheldon
runners_data.note: Veteran campaigner with solid recent placing record but needs career-best effort to win at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Soldierofthestorm will lead from the gate with no genuine pace rivals in this small field, allowing him to dictate terms throughout. Tapley, Hold Up La Colmine, Clotilda and Sheldon will all settle in behind the leader in a bunched group, creating a waiting game scenario. The lack of early pace pressure means Soldierofthestorm can bowl along at his own rhythm before the field closes late. This sustainable tempo strongly favours the proven front-runner Soldierofthestorm, as he can control the race without early pressure and kick clear when the closers make their moves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Soldierofthestorm maintains his usual prominent position and dictates a steady gallop
scenarios.body: He can string out his rivals over the final fences and use his tactical advantage to repel late challenges. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to save energy for a decisive move approaching the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners engage in a mid-race battle for position behind Soldierofthestorm
scenarios.body: This creates a more genuine test where class tells and the strongest stayers prevail in a driving finish. Tapley's proven winning form over this trip becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Soldierofthestorm sets too strong a pace trying to dominate completely
scenarios.body: The early leader weakens approaching the final fence, allowing the best closers to sweep past in the final furlong. Hold Up La Colmine's recent third places suggest he's ready to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupts the main contenders
scenarios.body: Sheldon or Clotilda can capitalize on others' misfortunes despite their moderate recent form. The veteran Sheldon's experience becomes valuable in a scrappy finish.

watchPoints.text: Soldierofthestorm's jumping accuracy early on - any mistake hands tactical advantage to his rivals
Tapley's inexperienced rider Isabelle Ryder making correct tactical decisions in running behind the leader
Hold Up La Colmine's ability to quicken when produced - recent thirds suggest he's knocking on the door
Clotilda showing ring-rust after 47-day absence following that fall at Wincanton
The pace becoming too slow mid-race which could set up a cavalry charge finish

races.name: Newton Abbot Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Taranis Dubh
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown style but Sean Bowen booking suggests yard confidence in this hold-up performer

runners_data.name: Duhallow Storm
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced unknown quantity from the Twiston-Davies/Honeyball combination with scope for improvement

runners_data.name: Ta Ra For Now Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with finishing concerns who hasn't run for 52 days and comes from a struggling yard

runners_data.name: Max d'Airy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing headgear with solid recent form on good ground and strong Paul Nicholls record

runners_data.name: Chocks Away
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can lead unopposed and has the tactical advantage in this pace scenario

runners_data.name: Quickkick
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with decent recent form and high TopSpeed figure suggesting finishing kick potential

runners_data.name: Jubilee Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with fade tendency who hasn't run for 77 days and comes from yard without recent winners

runners_data.name: Gospel Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with finishing concerns returning after 95-day break from an unfashionable stable

races.paceDynamic: Chocks Away looks the only natural early leader in this small field of eight, with his prominent style likely to see him dictate terms from the front. The majority of runners - Max d'Airy, Quickkick, Ta Ra For Now Jack, Jubilee Jack, and Gospel Moon - all prefer to be held up, meaning they'll be tracking behind a potentially uncontested leader. With such a high proportion of hold-up horses and limited pace pressure early, Chocks Away can set sustainable fractions before the back-markers need to make their moves. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can travel well in behind, while penalising horses that need a strong early gallop to be competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Chocks Away gets an easy lead and maintains stamina reserves for the finish
scenarios.body: The prominent runner faces minimal early pressure and can dictate ideal fractions, making it difficult for the hold-up brigade to peg back his advantage. His sustainable pace-setting style becomes a decisive tactical advantage when the chasers have ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Successful
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses can close the gap effectively in the final furlong despite the modest early pace
scenarios.body: Max d'Airy and Quickkick benefit from their superior ratings and ability to produce late kicks, with the Paul Nicholls and Hobbs/White yards knowing how to get horses ready. The patient tactics pay off as class tells in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknowns Taranis Dubh or Duhallow Storm shows significant improvement from their limited exposed form
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen's presence on Taranis Dubh suggests confidence from the Olly Murphy yard, while natural progression from either lightly-raced runner could catch the more exposed rivals. Their hold-up styles suit the likely pace scenario perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Chocks Away fails to sustain his effort and multiple hold-up horses finish strongly together
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where any of the back-markers could prevail, with minor differences in timing and position proving crucial. Form figures become less relevant as it turns into a tactical lottery.

watchPoints.text: Chocks Away's early fractions will be crucial - if he gets too easy a time in front, he becomes very hard to peg back
Max d'Airy wearing headgear suggests connections trying to sharpen him up for this hold-up role
Multiple hold-up horses including Ta Ra For Now Jack and Jubilee Jack have shown fade tendencies that could be exposed again
The lightly raced Taranis Dubh and Duhallow Storm represent unknown quantities who could outrun their odds with natural improvement
Sean Bowen's jockey choice on Taranis Dubh over other available rides suggests this Murphy runner is fancied despite limited form
